clue.text: Card game — what they have in Paris in den

indicators.note: in tells us the French word goes inside the word for a den

parts.note: a den or lair can be called a pit
the French for 'what' is que

explanation.surface: A card game whose name is explained by what the French have in their lair.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-language device is common: 'in Paris' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player card game played with a short pack of thirty-two cards.

clue.text: Quiet yearning to settle

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical term for quiet
an itch is a restless craving or yearning

explanation.surface: A quiet longing to put down roots.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch is to set up or fix in place, as when pitching a tent and settling there.

clue.text: Rodent burrowing under courtyard in ecologically significant area

indicators.note: burrowing under places the rodent below the courtyard in this down answer

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a college courtyard
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat tunnelling beneath a college courtyard in a protected habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'burrowing under' puts RAT below QUAD; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrat is a square plot marked out by ecologists for sampling plants or animals.

clue.text: Leap from the trance revitalised

indicators.note: revitalised suggests the letters are given new life in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone springs up after being revived from a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revitalised' rearranges THE TRANCE; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet jump in which the dancer crosses the feet in the air.

clue.text: Plant copper on front of street outside a court

indicators.note: outside says the symbol for copper wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: front of asks for the first letter of the word street

explanation.surface: A gardening tip about putting copper in front of a street near a courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces; the surface makes copper look like metal for a plant pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny desert plant that stores water in its fleshy stem.

clue.text: Wasp, regularly concealed pest

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word wasp

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A wasp keeping out of sight is a nuisance insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of WASP, AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are greenfly and blackfly, sap-sucking insects that damage plants.

clue.text: Bird that's quaint over terrace, one sending messages

indicators.note: over puts the word for quaint above the abbreviation in this down answer

parts.note: twee is British for quaint in an affected way
Ter. is an address abbreviation for terrace

explanation.surface: A bird that looks cute above a patio is in fact a message sender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird that's' points to the Twitter bird logo; the definition is someone posting on Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a person who posts short messages called tweets on Twitter.

clue.text: Drink as a loosener-up? Anything but

definitions.text: Drink as a loosener-up? Anything but

parts.words: Drink as a loosener-up? Anything but
parts.note: a strong drink to brace the nerves is the opposite of something that relaxes, since it makes rigid

explanation.surface: A drink meant to relax you that does the very opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: A strong drink taken to steady the nerves has a name meaning a thing that makes stiff, the reverse of a loosener.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff drink taken for courage is called this, and literally the word means something that makes rigid.

clue.text: Keep quiet when catching bird — time for sneaky movement

indicators.note: catching means the hush sound holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: sh is the command to keep quiet
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Instructions to stay silent while trapping a bird, as the moment for a stealthy approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'for' are links; the surface reads 'keep quiet' as an order rather than the letters SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is moving secretly and quietly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Spooner's joint repair as a symbol of new life

indicators.note: Spooner's asks us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the famous Oxford don

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
to fix something is to repair it

explanation.surface: A knee operation presented as a sign of fresh life.
explanation.walkthrough: A knee fix with its opening sounds swapped becomes 'fee nix', which sounds like the mythical bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix is the legendary bird reborn from its own ashes, a classic emblem of renewal.

clue.text: A stew of lamb stuffed into a bird, a WI dish?

indicators.note: stuffed into puts the article and the stewed meat inside the bird, just after its first letter

parts.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: stew of says the letters of lamb are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe for a bird stuffed with stewed lamb, as served by a women's club.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of 'a bird' is a link, and the A of 'a WI' ends the answer. The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's club famous for jam; the question mark flags that jambalaya is really Creole.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Creole rice dish; the WI tag is a playful nod to the Women's Institute's jam.

clue.text: Cleaner good, what? And a supervisor of others working

parts.note: a char is a charwoman, a British word for a domestic cleaner
eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cleaner is any good, and whether she supervises others.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR, short for charwoman, is everyday British English for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a worker in charge of a small team, ranking below a foreman.

clue.text: Component of feast of unusual food

indicators.note: Component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dish forming part of an unusual feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a soya food common in East Asian cooking.

clue.text: Sexually attractive companion in fur

parts.note: fit is British slang for sexually attractive
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A good-looking partner dressed in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitch is the fur of the polecat, used in garments and brushes.

clue.text: Assemble soldiers leaving finally to be hugged by the old man

indicators.note: to be hugged by says these pieces go inside the word for the old man

parts.note: the old man is slang for one's father
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word leaving

explanation.surface: Gather the troops, with one departing at last to embrace dad.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', the usual crossword soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgather is to meet together or gather in one place.

clue.text: Enclosing people in general in dull environment

indicators.note: the second in says the pronoun sits inside the word for dull
environment confirms the word for dull surrounds the other piece

parts.note: boring means dull
we can mean people in general, as in 'we all make mistakes'

explanation.surface: A remark about people being shut away in a drab setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosing' looks like a container signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bower is to enclose as in a leafy shelter, so bowering is enclosing.

clue.text: Little man like Tony Robinson gets an evening between Monday and Friday

definitions.text: an evening between Monday and Friday

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal British for little
the actor and TV presenter Tony Robinson was knighted, so he is a knight

explanation.surface: A short man resembling Tony Robinson gets a midweek evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link. Sir Tony Robinson is a British actor and presenter; the 'little man' nods to his small Baldrick role in Blackadder.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is any night on a working day rather than the weekend.

clue.text: Concert with others producing some hard stuff

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms in London
et al. is Latin shorthand for 'and others'

explanation.surface: A concert performed alongside fellow musicians yields some tough material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link. PROM is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms summer series in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometal is a heat-resistant cast iron, a very hard material.

clue.text: Poem with lots of hairy stuff entertaining father

indicators.note: entertaining means the hairy word hosts the abbreviation for father inside it

parts.note: maned means having a mane, a lot of hair
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A verse about a shaggy creature playing host to dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hairy poem, but 'with lots of hairy stuff' is one adjective, maned.
explanation.definitionFit: Manfred is a dramatic poem by Lord Byron about a guilt-ridden Faustian nobleman.

clue.text: King by the grace of God wanting external attention

indicators.note: external says the word for attention goes outside the abbreviation

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
DG abbreviates Dei gratia, Latin for 'by the grace of God', seen on British coins

explanation.surface: A monarch ruling by divine grace who craves outside attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link. D.G. appears on British coins after the monarch's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar was a tenth-century English king, so the name fits a monarch.

clue.text: Catch insect flying up in gadget

indicators.note: flying up in a down answer means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a snib is a catch or bolt on a door, mainly Scottish
bug is a general word for an insect

explanation.surface: Trapping a bug that has flown up into a piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIB plus BUG read upwards gives GUBBINS; 'in' is a link. GUBBINS is British slang for gadgetry or bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is British slang for a gadget or assorted bits of equipment.

clue.text: Report of mood being thoughtless

indicators.note: report of means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a vein is a mood or style, as in 'in a jocular vein'

explanation.surface: An account of someone's temper showing them to be unthinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain can mean conceited and self-absorbed, so heedless of others.

clue.text: Italian square dishing out a type of food you'd expect there?

clue.text: American schoolgirls who work together on a magazine maybe?

definitions.text: who work together on a magazine maybe?
definitions.meaning: people who jointly edit a publication, short for co-editors

explanation.definitionFit: Coeds are US female students at mixed colleges; split apart, the word reads as co-editors.

clue.text: After endless tedious work one gets cross — let's have a sausage!

clue.text: Bad editing will get one fired up

explanation.definitionFit: Ignited means set alight, and figuratively roused or excited.

clue.text: Design again seen to be bloody crude

clue.text: Secret police's state of equilibrium

parts.note: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: The secret police are said to be in a stable balance.
